title: Galois descent for a genuine semilinear matrix action
statement: Let K be any field, n a nonzero natural number, and b:G to GL_n(Ksep) locally constant for the Krull topology. Set T_g(M)=b(g) g(M) b(g) inverse. Assume T_1 is the identity on every matrix and T_g(T_h(M))=T_(gh)(M) for every g,h,M. Then there is a central simple K-algebra A and a Ksep-algebra splitting e:Ksep tensor_K A to Mat_n(Ksep) such that g(e(1 tensor a))=b(g) inverse e(1 tensor a) b(g) for every g,a. Conventions for central simple algebras and matrix splitting are those of [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect]. No cocycle or realization of a prescribed scalar defect is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 03R6 (Galois forms of matrix algebras), preceding Theorem 03R7; explicit finite Galois descent expanded from the parent construction

proof.text: Construct the actual invariant K-subalgebra S and its scalar-extension multiplication map by [def-sc-matrix-descent-invariants]. Its closure proofs use entrywise algebra homomorphisms, distributivity, conjugation cancellation and central scalar matrices.

Use [lem-sc-matrix-descent-scalar-map-bijective] with the local constancy and action hypotheses. AlgEquiv.ofBijective promotes the explicit map to an S-algebra equivalence e. The inverse is uniquely determined by that fixed bijective map.

Apply [lem-sc-matrix-form-central-simple] to the invariant algebra, e, and n≠0. Package its three proved properties with the concrete invariant carrier using AlgCat.of and CSA; no unspecified algebra witness is selected.

The scalar map sends 1 tensor a to the original invariant matrix a. The subtype property gives b(g) g(a) b(g) inverse = a. Apply the function M ↦ b(g) inverse M b(g) to this equality and cancel unit products by associativity. This yields g(a)=b(g) inverse a b(g), the required descent equation.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03R6 and Tag 03R2; concrete invariant construction, scalar extension, faithful-flatness/contraction descent, and unit cancellation
